commands.name: deliver start
commands.description: Prepare one isolated demand from its own intent using the existing engine and Seamwise. Present the concrete topology, scopes, evals and limits for initial owner alignment; never reuse another backlog.

commands.name: deliver authorize
commands.wraps: compose review/preview/materialize, Task-Spec gate, bind, loop
commands.example: cvg deliver authorize --demand health --reviewer owner --alignment-digest SHA256
commands.description: Explicit owner approval of the exact prepared alignment packet. Native products review and authorize leaves; Converge conducts dependency-ready tasks through independent acceptance and integrated proof. No publication or business acceptance.

commands.name: deliver resume
commands.description: Resume the same demand, workspace, authorization revisions and remaining limits. Never reset a leaf checkpoint or dispatch over a surviving command.

commands.name: deliver status
commands.description: Inspect the project-scoped demand without mutation. Revalidate current alignment and task authority; do not infer acceptance from a frontmatter flag.

commands.name: init
commands.description: Create the canonical tracked project control plane: .cvg/gate.yaml plus cvg/{brain,docs,swimlanes,tasks,execution,loop,receipts}. Non-clobbering, idempotent, and never writes credentials.

commands.name: capture
commands.description: Pass 0 gate — the BRD exit contract.

commands.name: intent
commands.description: Pass 1 gate — the tech-spec exit contract.

commands.name: structure
commands.description: Pass 2 gate — the ADR set.

commands.name: decompose --source <recipe>
commands.description: Compatibility alias for cvg compose prepare. Converge invokes Seamwise and never decomposes locally; --dir is rejected with a migration error.

commands.name: review --adversary <e[,e]>
commands.description: Pass 4 dispatch — a different-family adversary (or several, merged) attacks the plans; writes a provenance-stamped objection log.

commands.name: review --check
commands.description: Pass 4 gate — validates the stamped objection log (cross-family, resolutions, fork B, provenance).

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Engine readiness for Pass 4 dispatch (>=2 engines, >=1 cross-family).

commands.name: compose prepare --source <recipe>
commands.description: Invoke compatible external Seamwise transformations and stop at the explicit delivery-plan review boundary. It never records review, compiles a TaskPlan, or materializes Task-Specs.

commands.name: compose review --reviewer <name> --reason <text>
commands.description: Record human acceptance through Seamwise only. It never compiles a TaskPlan or invokes Task-Spec.

commands.name: compose preview
commands.description: Compile the reviewed Seamwise projection, validate it through Task-Spec plan, and write no Task-Spec Markdown.

commands.name: compose materialize
commands.description: Materialize the reviewed TaskPlan through Task-Spec, validate its receipt, and persist a digest-bound ConvergeCompositionReceipt/v1 with dispatch_authorized=false.

commands.name: compose status
commands.description: Read-only verification of composed state with exactly one safe next action.

commands.name: bind --task <spec>
commands.description: Pass 7 · Bind — verify one signed Task-Spec, select the initial intra-task topology, hash-bind the evidence slice, and emit portable path guards plus vendor adapter manifests.

commands.name: bind --check --task <spec>
commands.description: Re-check Task-Spec freshness, sign-off, context hashes, topology substance, ownership, and enforcement artifacts.

commands.name: loop --issue <id>
commands.description: Pass 8 · Loop — attempt/verify/repeat over ONE assigned task, bounded on three axes (iterations, wall-clock, tokens) with a stagnation detector. Each attempt runs in a fresh engine process; state is durable on disk. Never selects its own work. Lands in exactly one named terminal state; an error or an exhausted budget is never reported as success.

commands.name: loop --gate-only --issue <id>
commands.description: Read-only settlement verdict: resolve the task/profile and evaluate the gate without starting an engine or attempt.

commands.name: loop --estimate --issue <id>
commands.description: Read-only preflight showing the bounded iteration, wall-clock, token, lane, model, and verification ceiling before authorization.

commands.name: gate [--path P]
commands.description: The standing repo write fence — parses the tracked .cvg/gate.yaml policy and answers whether a path may be written. Read-only; the one fence a Task-Spec cannot widen. With no --path it reports whether the policy parses and is active.

commands.name: tasks plan --manifest <TaskPlan>
commands.description: Thin, read-only delegation to the independently installed Task-Spec engine. Converge passes the TaskPlan arguments unchanged and never derives or renders tasks.

commands.name: tasks new <slug>
commands.description: Create one Task-Spec in the resolved canonical backlog (cvg/tasks first; legacy tasks only when that existing layout is explicitly selected), append a created event, and rebuild state.

commands.name: tasks validate <spec>
commands.description: Structural lint + six-tier effort gate (leaf write-surface budgets; XL/XXL nodes need children). On success it refreshes the derived tasks/_state.yaml index.

commands.name: tasks validate --no-state <spec>
commands.description: Read-only structural validation for CI, audits, and sign-off checks; performs the same validation without refreshing tasks/_state.yaml.

commands.name: tasks gate <spec>
commands.description: Sign-off gate; refuses an XL/XXL node (dispatch its children, not the node).

commands.name: tasks gate --stamp <spec>
commands.description: Explicitly sign or re-seal the Task-Spec after the delegation gate passes. This is the mutating form; a plain tasks gate verdict remains read-only.

commands.name: tasks accept <spec>
commands.description: Post-execution acceptance.

commands.name: tasks dod <spec>
commands.description: Definition-of-Done + traceability matrix (every behavior B-N → its verifying eval); gates DOD=GAPS if a behavior is untraced. The 2026 agent-spec SOTA review artifact.

commands.name: tasks metrics [filters]
commands.description: Query the canonical append-only task lifecycle event index.

commands.name: tasks rebuild-state
commands.description: Re-derive the tasks/_state.yaml index from the frontmatter of every tasks/T-*.md, which is its only source of truth. `cvg init` builds it once and only when absent, and `tasks validate` refreshes it as a side effect, so a backlog edited by hand or by another tool can leave the derived index behind its specs. Safe to run at any time: the file is disposable by design and this rewrites it from scratch.

commands.name: register [--tracker T] [--no-stamp-refs]
commands.description: REGISTER ① — bridge signed-off Task-Specs onto a tracker board (1 spec = 1 issue, depends_on → blocked-by), then stamp a tracker_ref receipt back into each spec. Pluggable adapter github|linear|jira (default linear); the referee holds NO tracker credentials. Idempotent: re-runs upsert, never duplicate. --no-stamp-refs skips the write-back (CI-safe; the issue-side marker stays the key). On Linear, register also seeds native fields from existing frontmatter (assignee from execution_backend/agent via .cvg/identity, state from DAG position, subscribers directly from signed_off_by — assignee/state seed-once, subscribers union-merged) and honors an optional in-frontmatter projection: block (project/milestone/cycle/parent/template/sla; tracker-neutral, HMAC-safe). Structure projection (Initiative→Project→Milestones + append-only health) is opt-in via `cvg setup projection --enable` and OFF by default, so the base behavior is unchanged.

commands.name: register --check
commands.description: Gate the mapping is faithful: 1:1 count, every depends_on edge is one blocked-by link, no cycle, no un-gated leak. Read-only; the offline spec-side half runs with --dry-run.

commands.name: setup
commands.wraps: native (workspace + signing + doctor + adapter preflight + memory inspect)
commands.description: Readiness board for the canonical workspace, Tier-1 signing, engines, optional tracker integrations, and live document-memory status (READY/STALE/UNINITIALIZED/ERROR) with the exact next step. Code indexing stays planned and separate. Inspect only — cvg setup memory performs explicit init/migrate. Records CHOICES in .cvg/config, never credentials.

commands.name: setup signing [--force]
commands.description: Provision the repository Task-Spec HMAC key under Git-private state so signed specs reach Tier 1. Idempotent unless --force explicitly rotates the key.

commands.name: setup tracker <t> [--team K]
commands.description: Validate a tracker via preflight and record it as the default in .cvg/config; cvg register then defaults --tracker from it. For linear: export only LINEAR_API_KEY — the team is auto-discovered (a single team auto-selects; otherwise pass --team <KEY>, the key straight from the Linear URL), resolved to a UUID, and recorded. The API key is never stored.

commands.name: setup key [tracker]
commands.description: Store the tracker API key ONCE, outside the repository — OS keychain first (macOS Keychain / secret-tool), a 0600 file under ~/.config/converge/ as fallback. Reads the key from stdin, never argv (argv is visible in ps). .cvg/ keeps recording choices, never credentials; with no tracker argument it defaults from .cvg/config.

commands.name: setup repo [--branch b] [--url u]
commands.description: Link the repo to the tracker: derives a browsable blob base URL from the git remote (github/gitlab/bitbucket shapes) and records it as spec_base_url in .cvg/config, so every registered issue links back to the spec it was projected from. Branch-pinned; --branch/--url override.

commands.name: doctor runtime-contract [--runtime R]
commands.description: Attest what THIS host can actually enforce for Pass 7 — the isolation primitive (Seatbelt/Landlock/bubblewrap), whether the runtime binary is installed, and whether git worktrees work. Probes are conservative: an unprovable capability is reported absent, so a contract fails closed instead of assuming a control it never had. DEGRADED means the runtime claims prevent but only detect is provable.

commands.name: lane <intent> [--files N] [--paths p]
commands.description: Route work to the lane it earns. FAST = 5,7,8 (small reversible change); NORMAL = 1,2,5,7,8; FULL = 0-8. Deterministic and offline. It ROUTES but never WAIVES: touching auth/money/migrations/secrets/public-API or anything irreversible can never ride FAST, a new seam forces FULL, and no lane dispatches an unsigned spec. Every lane still ends at a green eval plus the path guard.

commands.name: verify --task <spec> [--judge E]
commands.description: Tier-2 adversarial verification: a DIFFERENT-FAMILY engine reads the diff, the spec's stated intent, and the holdout criteria the implementer never saw (never the worker's transcript) and is prompted to refute. Fails closed — a missing, malformed or timed-out verdict is never a pass. With no second engine the verdict is UNAVAILABLE: permitted for low blast radius, blocked for high unless --accept-unverified records the risk.

commands.name: setup harness
commands.description: Scaffold the project ROUTER (AGENTS.md): identity, folder map, where-to-look table, house rules — routing only, under ~50 lines. cvg never generates doctrine; auto-written context files measurably lower task success while raising cost. Per-task detail is delivered just-in-time by Pass 7B. Non-clobbering: an existing router is untouched and a .proposed sibling is written instead.

commands.name: setup identity [--list]
commands.description: Discover tracker identities as a ready-to-paste block. Read-only; an unmapped assignee remains a fail-soft optional enrichment.

commands.name: setup identity --map KEY=VAL [--map ...]
commands.description: Map execution_backend/agent choices to tracker identities in machine-local .cvg/identity. Keys are strictly backend:<engine>, agent:<role>, or default; writes are same-directory atomic and mode 0600.

commands.name: setup projection [--enable|--disable] [--project N] [--initiative N] [--milestones L]
commands.description: Opt in to T3 structure projection: records projection_enabled/project/initiative/milestones in .cvg/config so register's Step-0 pre-pass ensures Initiative→Project→Milestones (idempotent, by-name) and posts append-only health. Default DISABLED — a plain cvg register is byte-identical to today. Enabling preflights the configured tracker (projects need a live team). CHOICES only, never credentials.

commands.name: setup engines
commands.description: Per-engine readiness inside the setup surface — the same check as cvg doctor (>=2 engines, >=1 cross-family).

commands.name: setup memory [--vault PATH]
commands.description: Explicit document-memory preparation: install the pinned QMD module dependencies, then init or migrate. Ordinary cvg setup only inspects READY/STALE/UNINITIALIZED/ERROR and never auto-init, rebind, or refresh. --vault is init/migrate only; an existing native binding is left in place.

commands.name: memory init
commands.description: Bind a named external vault and build the local QMD/BM25 index. Refuses an unmigrated darkfactory binding. Default --root is the git toplevel of the consuming workspace; sidecar .darkfactory is not a different project. No Task-Spec required.

commands.name: memory migrate
commands.description: Import an existing darkfactory vault binding into native Converge memory, preserving human vault files. The only import path; init will not implicitly rebind.

commands.name: memory refresh
commands.description: Rebuild the local document-memory index after sources change. Never runs from cvg setup status.

commands.name: memory status
commands.description: Inspect native document-memory binding without mutation. Bounded ConvergeMemory/v1 JSON; execution_authorized is always false. Missing dependencies are ERROR and point at cvg setup memory.

commands.name: memory search
commands.description: Lexical BM25 search over the bound vault and canonical project sources. No Task-Spec required. Default --root is the consuming git repository.

commands.name: memory read
commands.description: Read a bounded slice of one memory source by repo-relative or vault/notes path. Evidence, not authorization.

commands.name: eval <spec>
commands.description: Run a Task-Spec's evals.

commands.name: lint
commands.description: Lint the backlog for overlaps/cycles.

commands.name: transition <id> <state>
commands.description: Move a task between statuses (locked + logged).

commands.name: next [--lane FULL|NORMAL|FAST]
commands.description: The descent conductor: derives which pass is current and which comes next from workspace evidence (each pass leaves artifacts in a known cvg/ folder — no stored state), prints the evidence board, the owning skill and its installed steering prompt (skills/<pass-skill>/references/pass-prompt.md — shipped with the package, never copied into the project), and the gate that closes the pass. Evidence presence is not a verdict: the cvg gates stay authoritative. The same engine's pre/post hooks (scripts/next-pass.sh pre|post N) enforce order fail-closed.

commands.name: next --guided [--lane FULL|NORMAL|FAST]
commands.description: Opt-in conversational view of the same evidence-derived conductor. It adds stable CONTINUE, EXPLAIN, INSPECT, and PAUSE choices at a pass boundary, instructs the agent to wait rather than infer CONTINUE, persists no chat state, and keeps NEXT_PASS as the final machine token.

commands.name: next pre <N> [--lane FULL|NORMAL|FAST]
commands.description: Public fail-closed pre-hook for the chat conductor. It refuses pass N until every earlier pass in the selected lane has left its required evidence and never replaces the pass's authoritative gate.

commands.name: next post <N>
commands.description: Public post-hook for the chat conductor. It verifies that pass N left its expected artifact, names the authoritative closing gate, and never treats artifact presence as a verdict.

commands.name: snapshot
commands.description: Build the deterministic, offline-safe, read-only cockpit contract from canonical repository evidence. The stable snapshotId excludes observation timestamps; artifacts are digest-bound references only, layout stays frontend-owned, optional domains report unavailable, and any core method/gate failure fails closed.

commands.name: doctor host
commands.wraps: native (pure bash — it must not depend on what it audits)
commands.description: Can THIS MACHINE run the delegation path? Checks git, the running bash, a bash 4+ (cvg lint needs one), python3, shellcheck and a sha256 tool — and for anything missing, NAMES THE VERBS IT BLOCKS. Written after shellcheck's absence produced this chain: safe-to-delegate passes --shellcheck-evals unconditionally, so the gate BLOCKED and no spec could be signed; cvg bind refuses an unsigned spec, so no execution profile was written; cvg loop then reported a missing runtime contract. Every message in that chain was correct and none of them was the cause, which sat three verbs upstream and cost an hour of bisecting — including a commit CI had passed, because CI installs shellcheck explicitly. Fails closed at exit 1 when a required tool is absent; DEGRADED when only an optional-but-load-bearing one is. Read-only.

commands.name: doctor evidence
commands.wraps: native (git ls-files --others over the cvg/ workspace)
commands.description: Can git show the floor the gates are standing on? Three parts of the method assume the workspace is version-controlled and none of them checks: Pass 4 stamps sha256 provenance over the plan FILES, Pass 8 settles by COMMITTING (staging from the capability envelope's fs.write grant, receipt written last), and `cvg lesson --immutable` proves teaching changed nothing by reading `git status --porcelain`. Found live: a workspace ran four green gates while its entire descent — BRD, tech-spec, six ADRs, eleven legs — was untracked, one `git clean` from gone, with every provenance claim resting on nothing. Reports per artifact folder and NAMES THE PASS at risk, because "3 untracked files" says less than "Pass 4 cannot prove provenance". Exploring without git is legitimate; settling is not, so NOT_GIT and UNTRACKED both fail closed at exit 1. Read-only.

commands.name: doctor plugin
commands.description: Answer the one question that makes every other verdict falsifiable: is the Converge a CONSUMING PROJECT loads the same Converge as its source? Compares the plugin install record's gitCommitSha against the marketplace clone's HEAD, and — the real claim — fingerprints the loaded tree against that clone's content. STALE means a project is running skills that are not the source, which is invisible otherwise: the cache path is keyed by version, so while VERSION does not move an update resolves to the same directory and keeps serving the stale copy. Also warns when you are running a different copy (a dev checkout) than projects load, because green gates there prove nothing about the plugin. UNMANAGED (exit 0) when there is no plugin install to compare. Read-only and offline by design — it never fetches, since a network-dependent doctor lies when offline.

commands.name: lesson [<file>] [--immutable <path>...]
commands.description: The teaching companion's gate — optional, invocable after ANY pass closes, and it never blocks the descent. Converge delegates the writing of every artifact but not the understanding of it: this gates the lesson a pass earned (all seven sections by exact name, 'what breaks downstream' on every component block, a non-empty decisions table, 3-5 check-yourself questions, and well-formed teaching-mode sections when the lesson declares modes). With --immutable <taught-artifact>... it proves teaching changed nothing it taught (clean git status; outside a repo it warns and skips). Discovery finds cvg/docs/lessons/ then legacy docs/lessons/ when no path is given; lessons accumulate by design, so more than one is a usage error naming them all rather than a non-deterministic newest-wins guess. Steering prompt: skills/pass-to-lesson/references/pass-prompt.md. What the gate cannot see stays human: that every emitted artifact is actually taught, that each rejected alternative is real, and that the owner restated it in their own words.

commands.name: ready [--all]
emits_tokens: frontier task list (+ a hidden-blocked count)
commands.description: List the DISPATCHABLE FRONTIER — status:ready specs whose every depends_on edge is already done. This is the surface a Manager selects work from, so it is dependency-aware by default: listing a spec whose inputs do not exist yet would dispatch work that cannot pass. Fails closed on a dangling or cyclic edge. --all restores the flat listing of every status:ready spec, blocked or not.

commands.name: help
commands.description: Human-readable command map.

commands.name: version
commands.description: Print the version.

commands.name: agent-context
commands.description: This machine-readable manifest (also: cvg manifest).
